_title: Trains from Germany to Italy (2026): Munich to Verona, Venice and Rome | WoW Train · glosx.app
_desc: How to go from Germany to Italy by train in 2026: direct EuroCity over the Brenner from Munich to Verona, Bologna and Venice, night trains, and where to change for Rome.
b1: By WoW Train · Updated July 2026 · 4 min read
b2: The train from Germany to Italy crosses the Alps over the Brenner Pass — one of the most scenic rail journeys in Europe. Direct EuroCity trains run from Munich to Venice in approximately 6 hours 30 minutes, passing through Innsbruck, the Dolomites and Verona.
b3: Routes from Germany to Italy by train
b4: The Brenner Pass — how the crossing works
b5: All direct trains from Munich to northern Italy cross the Alps via the Brenner Pass (1,371m), the lowest Alpine crossing in the Eastern Alps. The route goes through Innsbruck (Austria), over the pass, then descends through Bolzano and Trento into the Italian plain.
b6: The scenery through the Tyrolean Alps and the Dolomite foothills is exceptional. Unlike tunnel-only crossings, the Brenner route gives you panoramic mountain views for over two hours.
b7: How long does the train from Germany to Italy take?
b11: Munich to Rome: ~9–10h with one change at Bologna or Florence
b12: Frankfurt to Milan: ~7h with one change at Munich or Zurich
b13: Tips for the Munich to Italy train
b14: Book EuroCity seats in advance. Fares are fixed but seat reservations can fill up in peak summer months.
b15: Sit on the right side southbound for the best Brenner Pass and Dolomite views.
b16: Connect in Verona or Bologna for fast Frecciarossa services south to Rome or Florence.
b17: The night train is an option. The ÖBB Nightjet runs Munich–Venice and Munich–Rome overnight — you arrive rested without losing a day.

b21: Is there a direct train from Germany to Italy?
b22: Yes. Direct EuroCity trains run from Munich Hauptbahnhof to Venice, Verona and Bologna daily, crossing the Alps over the Brenner Pass via Innsbruck.
b23: How long does the train from Munich to Venice take?
b24: The direct EuroCity takes approximately 6 hours 30 minutes from Munich Hauptbahnhof to Venice Santa Lucia.
b25: Which train goes from Germany to Italy?
b26: EuroCity (EC) trains operated by DB and Trenitalia serve the Brenner corridor. The ÖBB Nightjet also runs overnight from Munich to Venice and Rome.
b27: Do I need to cross Austria to get from Germany to Italy by train?
b28: Yes. All direct trains between Bavaria and northern Italy pass through Innsbruck, Austria on the Brenner corridor. No visa is needed — all three countries are in the Schengen Area.
